findings.title: Function "do_stuff" has deeply nested control flow
findings.description: Nesting reaches depth 5 inside "do_stuff".
findings.impact: Deep nesting makes it hard to hold all the surrounding conditions in mind while reading the innermost logic.
findings.suggestedAction: Use guard clauses or early returns to flatten the outer conditions, or extract the inner block into a helper function.

findings.title: Function "do_stuff" takes 7 parameters
findings.description: "do_stuff" has 7 parameters, above the 5 generally considered easy to call correctly.

findings.suggestedAction: Consider whether some parameters are always passed together and could be grouped — though that depends on context.

findings.title: Unexplained number literal 7
findings.description: The number value 7 appears 2 time(s) without an explaining name.
findings.impact: A named constant documents intent and gives future readers — including the author — one place to change the value.
findings.suggestedAction: Extract 7 into a named constant that explains what it represents.

findings.title: "do_stuff" and "do_other_stuff" share identical structure
findings.description: These two functions have the same control-flow structure once identifier names are ignored.
findings.impact: Duplicated logic means every future fix or behavior change has to be made in more than one place, and it is easy to update one copy and forget the other.
findings.suggestedAction: Extract the shared structure into a single function that both call sites use.

findings.title: Import "os" appears to be unused
findings.description: "os" is imported but never referenced elsewhere in the file, based on name matching.
findings.impact: Unused imports add noise and can hide a missing dependency or a leftover from refactoring.
findings.suggestedAction: Remove the unused import if "os" is not referenced dynamically elsewhere.

findings.title: Bare except clause silently discards all errors
findings.description: An except/catch block (catching all exception types) has an empty or trivial body, so failures pass silently.
findings.impact: Swallowed exceptions hide real failures, making bugs far harder to diagnose later since there is no trace that anything went wrong.
findings.suggestedAction: Handle the specific exception type you expect, and at minimum log it — do not let failures disappear silently.
